camera.label: Theatrical
camera.description: Playful theatrical art-rock coverage: low wide-angle performance masters, face-forward close-ups, Dutch tilts, whip-pans, tracking, circling, and overhead views, with tender held portraits for quieter passages.
camera.guidance: Build a cheeky, theatrical performance through strong contrasts between low wide-angle masters, waist-up action, and wide-angle close-ups with the face large and expressive in frame. Let foreground hands, existing props, and softly blurred background activity add depth around the principal performer. Use purposeful whip-pans, backward tracking ahead of a moving performer, side tracking, and circling coverage for energetic passages; use held mirror portraits and a slow medium-to-close push-in for intimate passages. Match each choice to the scene's existing action, musical energy, and available duration. Place cuts on the supplied shot plan and performance beats. Across cuts, preserve each person's established position, orientation, posture, held objects, and ongoing action as the camera changes angle and framing. Keep facial expressions readable during vocal cues. Use the project's mapped subjects, locations, and props, adapting the camera setup to their actual staging. A held composition can carry a big gesture or a final pose; camera movement serves the performance.

performance.label: Theatrical
performance.direction: Use visibly theatrical art-rock acting with cheeky confidence, comic timing, and bold readable physical choices. In every shot with a visible performer, write a distinct motivated physical beat and its development: a pronounced head tilt, lifted chin and squared shoulders, cocked hip, mock-prim posture, open-palm flourish, rhythmic shoulder bounce, purposeful strut, mock bow, or playful turn. Choose the beat to express this shot's lyric or story intention within the authored action, framing, available time, and established props. Carry posture and movement continuously across cuts, then develop the new acting beat from that inherited state. A walking performance includes an expressive change of posture, head, shoulders, or hands as well as the stride. A held camera records active theatrical acting; camera speed controls camera travel, while character speed controls the pace and extent of physical movement. At lower speeds, use deliberate emphatic gestures with clear setup and payoff. Supporting performers react individually in character and instrumentalists move in time with their parts. Match assigned vocal delivery to the words with sly, teasing, mock-regal, gleeful, defiant, or triumphant intent. Tender story beats retain clearly legible, deliberate theatrical expression. Preserve exact words, assigned performers, vocal windows, scene action, cast, and physical continuity. Fit the acting to the visible frame and the scene's explicit direction.

facial.label: Theatrical
facial.description: Big, cheeky expressions with comic timing and tender quieter beats
facial.direction: Use big, playful, cheeky theatrical facial acting. For each readable face in every shot, describe a clear opening expression, a visible change motivated by the words or story beat, and the expression it lands on. Give the eyes or brows a pronounced action paired with a distinct smile, cheek, head, or gaze change: brows shooting up into mock alarm before a broad knowing grin, a cocked eyebrow and conspicuous sideways glance turning into a slow wink, or exaggerated prim composure breaking into delighted laughter. Choose a different fitting progression as the performance develops. Carry the previous shot's ending expression across the cut and visibly develop it. Give each readable supporting face its own story-motivated reaction, such as frozen astonishment, skeptical raised brow, deadpan pride, or delighted disbelief. Size expressions to the shot so the viewer can read them immediately. Tender passages use a deliberate gaze change, lifted inner brows, and an openly warm smile with the same clarity of intention. Keep performance words and vocal articulation aligned to their assigned cue windows, with natural resting mouth shapes between cues and occasional natural blinks. Emotion words in a vocal tag accompany concrete visible acting in the surrounding shot prose.
